name: brisk_walking
source_authority: Fit India Movement (MoHFW & MYAS, Govt of India)
modifications: Short 10-15 minute bouts after meals to assist glucose blunting (ICMR-NIN 2024)
Wear supportive footwear with cushioned insoles on even flat ground
Maintain conversational pace (able to speak without breathlessness)
alternatives: Seated arm ergometer or gentle seated marching
Gentle stretching and mobility flow
Stationary recumbent cycling
guideline_notes: Fit India standard cardio protocol: 30-45 minutes daily moderate aerobic activity ('Fitness Ki Dose, Aadha Ghanta Roz'). Ideal for glycemic and hypertension management.
citation: Fit India Age-Appropriate Fitness Protocols 18-64 Years, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports & MoHFW, Govt of India, Section 4.1

name: squats
source_authority: Fit India Movement (MoHFW & MYAS, Govt of India)
modifications: Chair-supported shallow squats (limit knee bend to 45 degrees)
Wall slide with exercise ball supporting the lumbar spine
Keep knees tracking behind toes and avoid deep flexion past 90 degrees
alternatives: Glute bridges (floor-based movement, removes knee shear force)
Seated straight-leg raises to build quadriceps without joint loading
Gentle flat-surface walking
guideline_notes: Fit India lower body functional movement. Promotes bone density and leg endurance. Knee pain patients must limit flexion range.
citation: Fit India Age-Appropriate Fitness Protocols 18-64 Years, MoHFW & MYAS, Section 4.2

name: heavy_deadlifts
modifications: Bodyweight hip hinge practice with neutral lumbar spine
Light dumbbell Romanian deadlift with continuous rhythmic breathing (strictly no breath-holding)
alternatives: Bird-dog exercise on a soft mat (strengthens posterior chain with zero axial spine loading)
Glute bridges on mat for posterior glute/hamstring engagement
Brisk walking with active core bracing
guideline_notes: WHO & ACSM Clinical Contraindication: High-load maximal resistance exercises causing acute Valsalva-induced systolic spikes (>200 mmHg) are strictly contraindicated in unmonitored hypertension.
citation: WHO Guidelines on Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour 2020, Section: Adults with Chronic Conditions

name: jumping_jacks
source_authority: Fit India Movement (MoHFW & MYAS, Govt of India)
modifications: Low-impact step-jacks (step one foot out to the side without jumping)
Rhythmic arm raises while walking in place
alternatives: Brisk walking with synchronized arm pumping
Low-impact steady marching in place
Stationary cycling at a comfortable cadence
guideline_notes: High-impact landing creates 3-4x bodyweight ground reaction forces. Unsuitable for active knee/ankle pain or unmanaged stage 2 hypertension.
citation: Fit India Fitness Assessment Protocol (Age 18-64), Section 3.3

name: overhead_press
modifications: Seated neutral-grip dumbbell press with light resistance
Limit movement range below 90 degrees shoulder abduction
alternatives: Resistance band pull-aparts for scapular stability
Incline chest press with light dumbbells
Gentle wall-crawls and shoulder pendulum mobility exercises
guideline_notes: Overhead loading can exacerbate rotator cuff impingement and trigger Valsalva response. Patients with stage 2 hypertension should avoid sustained overhead lifting.
citation: WHO Guidelines on Physical Activity 2020 & Clinical Exercise Guidelines for Hypertension

name: crunches
source_authority: Fit India Movement (MoHFW & MYAS, Govt of India)
modifications: Pelvic tilts on a flat mat with knees bent
Deadbug exercise focusing on transverse abdominis engagement
alternatives: Bird-dog on all fours (safe isometric core stabilization)
Forearm plank from knees with neutral spine
Standing isometric ab bracing during daily walks
guideline_notes: Repetitive spinal flexion under compressive load aggravates lumbar disc herniation. Isometric stabilization is preferred for spine safety.
citation: Fit India Age-Appropriate Fitness Protocols 18-64 Years, Section 4.3

name: running
source_authority: Fit India Movement (MoHFW & MYAS, Govt of India)
modifications: Brisk walking intervals (walk fast 2 mins, gentle walk 1 min)
Walk on level grass or soft track rather than hard pavement
alternatives: Brisk outdoor walking or treadmill incline walking at low speed
Stationary cycling with smooth pedal stroke
Gentle swimming or shallow-water walking
guideline_notes: Vigorous aerobic activity. Individuals with joint pain or cardiac history should maintain low-impact cardio alternatives.
citation: Fit India Movement Protocols, MoHFW & MYAS, Section 4.1

name: gentle_yoga
source_authority: Ministry of AYUSH & MDNIY (Common Yoga Protocol, Govt of India)
modifications: Use yoga blocks and wall support for balance
Avoid deep twists or inversions if blood pressure is elevated
alternatives: Chair yoga and seated spinal mobility
Guided diaphragmatic breathing and relaxation
guideline_notes: Ministry of AYUSH Common Yoga Protocol: Safe, gentle loosening practices (Sadilaja) and restorative asanas for all age groups.
citation: Common Yoga Protocol (CYP), Ministry of AYUSH & MDNIY, Govt of India, Chapter 3

name: tadasana
source_authority: Ministry of AYUSH & MDNIY (Common Yoga Protocol, Govt of India)
modifications: Keep feet hip-width apart rather than joined for better base of support
Keep heels on the floor if balance is unsteady
alternatives: Seated posture alignment in a firm chair
Gentle wall-supported standing alignment
guideline_notes: Promotes physical and mental stability; corrects posture and stretches thoracic spine.
citation: Common Yoga Protocol, Ministry of AYUSH, Section 3.1

name: vajrasana
source_authority: Ministry of AYUSH & MDNIY (Common Yoga Protocol, Govt of India)
modifications: Place a folded blanket or yoga cushion between heels and buttocks
Place a small rolled towel under ankles
alternatives: Sukhasana (Easy seated pose) on a cushion
Seated chair posture with upright spine
guideline_notes: The only asana recommended to be practiced immediately after meals to stimulate digestion. Avoid in acute knee joint inflammation.
citation: Common Yoga Protocol, Ministry of AYUSH & MDNIY, Section 3.7

name: bhujangasana
source_authority: Ministry of AYUSH & MDNIY (Common Yoga Protocol, Govt of India)
modifications: Sarala Bhujangasana (Sphinx pose on forearms with gentle arch)
Keep elbows slightly bent and avoid hyperextension of lumbar spine
alternatives: Makarasana (Crocodile pose) for passive spinal relaxation
Seated gentle thoracic arch in chair
guideline_notes: Strengthens back muscles and improves chest expansion. Effective for bronchial asthma and mild back stiffness.
citation: Common Yoga Protocol, Ministry of AYUSH & MDNIY, Section 3.11

name: makarasana
source_authority: Ministry of AYUSH & MDNIY (Common Yoga Protocol, Govt of India)
modifications: Adjust width of feet to comfortable distance
Place a thin cushion under lower abdomen if lumbar lordosis causes tension
alternatives: Shavasana (Corpse pose)
Side-lying resting posture
guideline_notes: Restorative prone posture. Highly recommended for patients with hypertension, stress, and lower back tension.
citation: Common Yoga Protocol, Ministry of AYUSH & MDNIY, Section 3.13

name: setubandhasana
source_authority: Ministry of AYUSH & MDNIY (Common Yoga Protocol, Govt of India)
modifications: Place a yoga block beneath sacrum for supported passive bridge
Keep lift moderate without straining cervical neck spine
alternatives: Floor glute bridges with head flat on mat
Pelvic tilts on mat
guideline_notes: Relieves backache, stretches neck and chest, calms brain and helps alleviate stress and mild hypertension.
citation: Common Yoga Protocol, Ministry of AYUSH & MDNIY, Section 3.14

name: anulom_vilom
source_authority: Ministry of AYUSH & MDNIY (Common Yoga Protocol, Govt of India)
modifications: Perform without breath retention (Kumbhaka) in hypertension or cardiac conditions
Maintain smooth, rhythmic 1:1 inhalation-exhalation ratio
alternatives: Simple deep diaphragmatic breathing
Bhramari pranayama
guideline_notes: Principal calming pranayama. Reduces sympathetic activity, lowers heart rate and blood pressure, improves mental clarity. Safe for all patients.
citation: Common Yoga Protocol, Ministry of AYUSH & MDNIY, Section 4.1

name: bhramari_pranayama
source_authority: Ministry of AYUSH & MDNIY (Common Yoga Protocol, Govt of India)
modifications: Practice without pressing tragi if ears feel sensitive
Gentle low-pitch humming without forceful exhalation
alternatives: Nadi Shodhana pranayama
Gentle rhythmic exhalation counting
guideline_notes: Generates endogenous nitric oxide in paranasal sinuses. Alleviates stress, anger, and anxiety; beneficial in mild hypertension.
citation: Common Yoga Protocol, Ministry of AYUSH & MDNIY, Section 4.2

name: plank
source_authority: Fit India Movement (MoHFW & MYAS, Govt of India)
modifications: Knee plank (knees on mat to reduce lever arm and intra-thoracic pressure)
Incline forearm plank against a sturdy table or wall
Short 10-second holds with continuous breathing (avoid breath-holding)
alternatives: Bird-dog on all fours
Deadbug on mat
Glute bridges
guideline_notes: Core endurance benchmark in Fit India. Hypertensive patients must not perform prolonged isometric breath holds.
citation: Fit India Age-Appropriate Fitness Protocols 18-64 Years, Section 4.3

name: pushups
source_authority: Fit India Movement (MoHFW & MYAS, Govt of India)
modifications: Wall push-ups (standing arms-length from wall, low joint load)
Incline push-ups on kitchen counter or bench
Knee push-ups on soft mat
alternatives: Resistance band chest press
Seated dumbbell chest press with neutral grip
Isometric chest press with palms joined
guideline_notes: Fit India upper body endurance standard. Regress to wall or knee pushups if shoulder or wrist pain is reported.
citation: Fit India Age-Appropriate Fitness Protocols 18-64 Years, Section 4.2
